description: Somos un equipo de 6 estudiantes de Ingeniería Mecatrónica de la ESPOL y representantes del nuevo capítulo IEEE AESS. Combinamos habilidades en programación, electrónica, diseño 3D y simulación. 🚀
summary:
On deep-space missions to Mars (140 million miles from Earth), astronauts face five lethal spaceflight hazards—including Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS in 70% of crews), 1.5% monthly bone mineral loss, and sudden solar radiation spikes (SPE/CME). Yet medical emergencies face up to a 40-minute round-trip communication delay or signal blackouts, making real-time flight surgeon support from Houston impossible.

We developed ASTRIA (HRP Health Monitor), an offline-first, autonomous clinical triage web platform and early-warning system designed for non-physician astronauts. ASTRIA processes automatic sensor telemetry and manual diagnostic inputs through a deterministic rule engine grounded in NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Evidence Books, NASA-STD-3001 limits, HERA isolation studies, and CSA data. It visualizes status across a color-coded anatomical Body Map, multi-parameter Trend Charts, and delivers step-by-step countermeasures—queuing medical reports locally during blackouts and synchronizing automatically once links return. Moreover, ASTRIA scales to remote rural clinics on Earth without internet access.
details:
1. WHAT ASTRIA DOES & HOW IT WORKS

ASTRIA (HRP Health Monitor) is an offline-first, autonomous clinical triage platform and early-warning system built for long-duration spaceflight (ISS, Artemis Lunar Base at 1/6 g, and Mars Base at 3/8 g) and isolated terrestrial environments.

Instead of a single cluttered screen, ASTRIA organizes autonomous crew healthcare into six specialized modules:

- Mission Dashboard: Automatically adjusts latency rules (up to 20 min one-way / 40 min round-trip on Mars) and flags priority alerts across the squad (Optimal, Warning, Critical).

- Crew Profiles & Interactive Body Map: Clicking any crewmember displays an interactive SVG anatomical map color-coded across four physiological systems (Neurovisual, Cardiovascular, Musculoskeletal, and Immune/Respiratory).

- Telemetry Log & Self-Exam Guides: Combines automated wearable telemetry (resting heart rate, sleep hours, cumulative radiation in mSv, cabin O2) with manual clinical inputs (blood pressure, glucose, temperature, mood, visual changes, and ocular ultrasound/OCT demonstration records) alongside built-in self-examination protocols.

- Multi-Parameter Trend Charts: Tracks longitudinal evolution of radiation exposure, sleep architecture, bone mineral density demineralization, cardiovascular vitals, and cabin oxygen.

- Daily Routines & Crew Feedback: Gamifies preventive countermeasures (resistive exercise, hydration, cognitive journaling, pre-EVA checklists) into a Mission Readiness score and crew logbook.

- Verified NASA & Partner Reference Repository: Provides offline access to primary space medicine documentation.

2. SCIENTIFIC VALIDITY & STEP-BY-STEP COUNTERMEASURES

Rather than relying on a black-box LLM that could hallucinate life-critical medical advice, ASTRIA uses a deterministic rule-based triage engine (triageService.js and telemetryLogic.js) grounded in NASA HRP Evidence Books, NASA-STD-3001 (250 mSv 30-day hematological limits), HERA 45-day isolation studies, and CSA dosimetry. When thresholds are breached, ASTRIA prescribes concrete protocols for non-physician astronauts—such as retreating to water and RFX1 polyethylene storm shelters during SPE/CME events, scheduling Russian Chibis (LBNP) negative-pressure suit sessions for SANS fluid shifts, or applying LED phototherapy and Veggie botanical care for circadian misalignment.

3. DUAL IMPACT & TERRESTRIAL SCALABILITY

Because microgravity physiological adaptations mirror accelerated aging, osteoporosis, and cardiovascular deconditioning on Earth, ASTRIA has immediate terrestrial value. Its lightweight, zero-dependency offline architecture can be deployed today by public health ministries, NGOs, and rural medical brigades in remote areas (such as rural communities outside Guayaquil, the Ecuadorian coast, the Galápagos Islands, and disaster zones) to triage patients without internet connectivity.

4. TOOLS, ARCHITECTURE & ENGINEERING FACTORS

- Frontend: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, interactive SVG mapping, and Web Storage API (localStorage) for persistent offline report queuing.

- Backend: Native Node.js REST API (built on node:http with zero external runtime dependencies for maximum reliability in mission-critical environments), featuring an idempotent asynchronous batch synchronization pipeline (/api/reports/sync).

- Factors Considered: Zero cloud dependency during communication blackouts, low computational footprint for spacecraft and rural edge devices, cognitive ergonomics for stressed non-medical operators, and zero cost of deployment.

5. ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

In compliance with NASA Space Apps Challenge rules, we declare that generative AI (LLM assistant) was utilized during development for code structuring, debugging, UI text refinement, pitch deck layout generation, and AI text-to-speech voice narration for our 30-second video demonstration. All clinical thresholds and triage rules were verified against official NASA and CSA documentation.
